item.title: Expressions in Metal Exhibition — Thu Aug 20, 12:00 AM — Petaluma Arts Center
item.description: Expressions in Metal In the Main Gallery, Expressions in Metal brings together nine Northern California artists who treat metal not as a static material but as a living language. Curated by Vicky Kumpfer, this exhibition highlights a range of contemporary practices rooted in metalwork. Some artists forge, cast, or weld, honoring the discipline's long lineage of craftsmanship. Others push the material into unexpected territories, experimenting with surface, scale, and form. Across the exhibition, metal is bent, stretched, pierced, patinated, and even coaxed into gestures that contradict its reputation for hardness. What emerges is a chorus of works that carry the traces of heat, pressure, repetition, and decision-marks that become expressive in themselves. These expressions remind us that metal, for all its industrial associations, will record touch, hold history, and reflect the light around it. item.title: Marin Farmers Markets — Thu Aug 20, 8:00 AM — Marin Veterans' Memorial Auditorium
item.description:
Price: Free
Sponsor: Marin Center
Explore the bounty of summer at the Marin Farmers Markets. Taste vine-ripened tomatoes, corn that was picked that morning, and peaches so juicy you have to bend over just to get a bite. Farm-fresh eggs, grass-fed beef, artisan c heeses, raw milk, and freshly baked breads complete the shopping exper ience. Specialty prepared foods and handmade art add to the magic of the market.
Enjoy the intimate feeling of the Thursday Marin Farmers Market, an ideal place to meet for lunch and pick up fresh produce for the weekend. Discover the abundance and diversity of product at the celebrated Sunday Marin Farmers Market, the third largest farmers market in California. Turn your dollar into a vote for local sustainable agriculture, shrink your eco-footprint, and revive the feeling of being intimate ly connected to your food by meeting your farmers face-to-face. The market takes place rain or shine.
www.aginstitutemarin.org
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Dem

Ticket Info:
Sponsor: Marin Center
Link: http://www.marincounty.org/depts/cu
The Frank Lloyd Wright-designed Marin County Civic Center is a national- and state-designated historic landmark. Ninety minute docent-led tours of the Civic Center are offered every Wednesday and Friday at 10:30 am, leaving from the second floor Café, Room 233. The cost is $10 adults and $5 seniors and students. No reservations are required. Groups of ten or more can arrange a private docent tour by calling the Visitor Services Office at \(415\) 473-3762.

item.description:

Over one spectacular weekend, you'll explore five distinct experiences alongside national culinary stars and celebrated local artisans, all set against the backdrop of open-flame cooking and world-class Sonoma wines. Ignite your senses across two spectacular worlds. Step onto the pool deck, where the rich aroma of live-fire cooking fills the air and chefs plate flame-kissed proteins right before your eyes. Discover the magic of ice dyeing in this fun, hands-on workshop! During the evening session, you’ll learn how to fold, arrange, and apply fiber-reactive dyes over ice to create unique, watercolor-like patterns. Your dyed pieces will process overnight as the ice slowly melts, blending colors in surprising and beautiful ways.Return the following afternoon to rinse and reveal your one-of-a-kind creations. Each participant will receive two cotton tea towels to dye and may also bring one pre-washed 100% cotton T-shirt to customize. No experience is necessary, and all dyeing supplies are provided.

item.description: Expressions in Metal In the Main Gallery, Expressions in Metal brings together nine Northern California artists who treat metal not as a static material but as a living language. Curated by Vicky Kumpfer, this exhibition highlights a range of contemporary practices rooted in metalwork. Some artists forge, cast, or weld, honoring the discipline's long lineage of craftsmanship. Others push the material into unexpected territories, experimenting with surface, scale, and form. Across the exhibition, metal is bent, stretched, pierced, patinated, and even coaxed into gestures that contradict its reputation for hardness. What emerges is a chorus of works that carry the traces of heat, pressure, repetition, and decision-marks that become expressive in themselves. item.description:
Price: Free Sponsor: Marin Center
Explore the bounty of summer at the Marin Farmers Markets. Taste vine-ripened tomatoes, corn that was picked that morning, and peaches so juicy you have to bend over just to get a bite. Farm-fresh eggs, grass-fed beef, artisan c heeses, raw milk, and freshly baked breads complete the shopping exper ience. Specialty prepared foods and handmade art add to the magic of the market. Discover the abundance and diversity of product at the celebrated Sunday Marin Farmers Market, the third largest farmers market in California. Turn your dollar into a vote for local sustainable agriculture, shrink your eco-footprint, and revive the feeling of being intimate ly connected to your food by meeting your farmers face-to-face. item.title: Island Time at the Paper Mill? — Sun Aug 23, 1:00 PM — Paper Mill Creek Saloon
item.description:
In an unlikely Western migration, five bands from the tropical island of St. John USVI find themselves here in Northern California without a home. From the white sand, rum-soaked beaches of the Caribbean to the Coastal Redwoods, we can’t even begin to explain how or why (truth is, they were among the acts booked at the sadly imploded Freak Nest festival in SF). But trust us. St. John knows how to rock. Join us for an afternoon in the saloon for a splash of psychedelic, island-inspired funk, rock and pop direct from the Virgin Islands. Headliner The Orange Peels was a regular in the SF music scene before its founders moved to St. John for 5 years. Now they’re back, and they brought their friends. PuZL, Mother Goat and the Housewives of St. John are all dropping new music in coming days.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.description:

Monday Jazz Jam is a welcoming, musician-friendly evening where players can sit in, listeners can enjoy a relaxed club atmosphere, and the music moves naturally from swinging standards to blues, ballads, Latin grooves, and spontaneous improvisation.
Together, they’ll anchor the night with taste, experience, and musical flexibility, giving guest musicians a strong foundation to step up and join the jam. Whether you’re a horn player, vocalist, guitarist, percussionist, bassist, pianist, or simply a jazz lover, this is a night built around community, creativity, and live interaction.
Musicians play free and get dinner, making this one of Vallejo’s most inviting weekly gatherings for working players, students, seasoned improvisers, and music fans alike.
The jam runs from 7 PM to 10 PM, with doors and dinner beginning at 6 PM.
